title: MetaCan screening label
description: The output contract for one screened work. protocol/rubric.md instructs both machine screeners and both human coders to return exactly this. It did not exist until 2026-07-11 (DEVIATIONS.md D9): the rubric pointed at a file that was not in the repository, and the schema was inlined in the prompts instead. A locked instrument that references a missing file is not locked.

id.description: OpenAlex work ID, bare (W123456789), not the full URL.

tier.description: T1 core metaresearch; T2 adjacent (STS, LIS, research infrastructure); T3 contextual (policy, editorials: mapped, never pooled with T1/T2); OUT otherwise. The in-scope decision that gates the corpus is tier in {T1, T2}.

genre.description: OpenAlex `type` is unreliable and this field is commentary-heavy, so genre is screened rather than inherited.

about_ca.description: Is the work ABOUT the Canadian research system, irrespective of author location? This is the secondary estimand (PROTOCOL s3) and is recorded separately from the primary.

confidence.description: The screener's own confidence. The rubric requires `low` whenever the abstract is missing and the judgement rests on the title alone. NB (DEVIATIONS.md D1): the pilot harness withheld five of the eight fields the rubric mandates, so pilot confidence values reflect a title-and-abstract screen, not the specified one.

reason.description: Optional. One clause naming the rubric criterion that decided it. Required when confidence is `low` or tier is T2 (the contested boundary).
